action_summary: Measures the owner's claim that solved instant learning implies solved computer use, and finds a defect upstream of every learning option: the stood-up check treated `python -m unittest` exit 0 as a verdict, but unittest collects nothing from a pytest-style module and exits 0. 943 of 2592 tracked test files (36.38%) have that shape; two were run both ways (unittest: 0 tests/OK; pytest: 10 and 4 passed). On a constructed project the legacy path accepted a deliberately broken `return None` edit; the repaired check refuses it and still accepts the original. Also audits the five durable experience stores against the training-signal contract of ASCENT and Experience Distillation: 0 of 71 rows are admissible and no store records a single failure. Claims no capability, flips no family, moves no benchmark.
expected_parent_change: A stood-up check reports a verdict only when it executed at least one test; zero collection, collection error and missing dependency are distinct refusals rather than a pass.
expected_parent_frontier_change: The check admission path no longer stamps verified on an untested edit. No capability is registered and no family is flipped.
falsification_condition: The repaired check accepts a broken edit in a pytest-style project, refuses a genuinely passing unittest project, reports a verdict when nothing ran, or an existing consumer of the tool regresses.
stop_condition: The broken-edit counterfactual is refused and the passing controls are accepted; 24 new tests pass; the two existing consumer suites and the compatibility four suites add no new failure; the unified verifier passes 33/33; repo-integrity static passes; the required referee is green; no capability, family, benchmark or terminal credit is claimed.
explicit_user_authorization: Paraphrase, not a quotation: the owner asks whether solved instant learning implies solved computer use and asks for the smartest real next step. This action changes no law, no protected guard, and no terminal truth.
